answers.H1: The corrected target is a sufficient probe plan or an indistinguishable model set demonstrating that no permitted plan can meet the regret tolerance. A valid impossibility certificate connects indistinguishability to the absence of a common acceptable action; use a pair when sufficient. A pair alone can miss the obstruction: the correction gives three indistinguishable models whose zero-loss action sets are {a,b}, {a,c}, and {b,c}. Every pair shares an acceptable action, but all three share none. Under the declared finite models, deterministic actions, and loss table, every action has worst-case regret 1, so identical responses to every permitted probe prevent certification below 1. Source: decision-certificate-correction.md.
answers.H2: When constructing the finite model–calibration family, check whether each indistinguishable model set has a common action meeting the regret tolerance, including sets larger than pairs. This is proposed work, not completed research. Source: decision-certificate-correction.md, especially its corrected target and next action.
